# DeepSeek Harness - Tool Router

Lazy tool discovery for DSH: hides every tool schema from the model's prefill
and reveals exactly on
e tool on demand through a **decision model API**.

- **Prefill cost:** one small `find_tool` schema instead of every mounted tool
(26 schemas on a defa

ult Standard profile — see Why?).
- **Stage 0** — full-surface send: every mounted tool (≤ 24) carri

es a
160-char criterion, ordered by a stopword-filtered lexical rank (the rank
only bounds pathologi

cal mounts — d1-omni does not saturate as the choice
count grows; see Why?).
- **Stage 1** — one `PO

ST /v1/systemone` to the decision model API: a
`bestTool` choice plus a `usable` question kept as te

lemetry only
(~235–500 tokens, ~6–7 s on-device).
- **Stage 2** — accept iff `confidence >= 0.70`: r

eturn the winner's JSON
Schema and reveal exactly that one tool; otherwise return a
**probability-or

dered shortlist** whose reason names the closest match, so
the model can retry with that exact tool

name (or send an empty request to
get the whole catalog). Exact tool-name requests skip the decision

call and
reveal instantly.
## Why?

Fresh session, first message, server-reported `usage.prompt_tokens` —
the DSH **Standard preset** (t

he platform default) versus this plugin's
`no-prefill` preset:

| Cost before the first word | Standard | no-prefill |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prefill tokens | **6,559**

| **283** |
| System prompt | 5,816 chars | 372 chars |
| Tool schemas shipped up front | **26 schem

Standard makes the model ingest a 5.8k-character system prompt plus **every**
mounted tool schema —

6,559 tokens — before it emits a single word, and pays
it again on every subsequent turn. `no-prefil

l` ingests 283 tokens (**23×
less**, 96% smaller prefill): a slim persona plus the single `find_tool

`
schema. On the measured backend that difference was ~40 s versus ~14 min of
prompt evaluation for

measured backend that difference was ~40 s versus ~14 min of
prompt evaluation for the first reply.
What that buys you:

- **Latency** — time-to-first-word scales with the whole tool shelf today.
Reveal-on-demand makes it

scale with the tool you actually call.
- **Context budget** — 6.5k tokens of standing preamble is 6

.5k tokens you
don't have for code, conversation, and results. On a 32k window that's ~20%
of the mo

del's world spent before work starts.
- **Reliability on small models** — a model reading 26 schemas

behaves like a
model reading 26 instructions it must never violate. One schema at a time is
one sch

ema to follow; the rest of the shelf doesn't exist for it.
- **Pay for what you use** — a turn that

calls no tool costs 283 tokens
instead of 6,559. A turn that calls one tool reveals that one schema

once;
the other 25 are never sent.

If a session ends up using most tools anyway, the gap narrows — but the unused
half of the shelf is
exactly what a default profile charges for from word one.
## What the bundle patch declares
`plugin/cordis.patch.yml` (applied when the bundle is selected):

1. **`preset-no-prefill`** — an agent preset whose composition is only
`persona` + `dsh-tool-router`

. The persona tells the model: no tools are
declared; call `find_tool` first — and if a result carri

es no schema,
retry with an exact tool name or an empty request instead of giving up.
It also states

the reveal rule from PR #2: every tool already used in the
session stays available for the rest of

it (including after a host
restart), so an answer carrying `"already_available": true` means *call i

t
directly, do not ask again*.
2. **Host tool rows enabled** — `tool-bash`, `tool-fs`, `tool-fs-sear

ch`,
`tool-todo`, `tool-web` flipped to `disabled: false`, plus a `present`
row inserted. Discovery

needs the tools to exist somewhere; preset-scoped
registrations shadow host ones, so other presets k

eep their own behavior.
The slim preset keeps the Agent Presets page showing only `find_tool`.
## Prerequisites

- DSH with the bundle mechanism (`dsh.bundle.patch`) — available since
`0.1.1-rc.2`; verified agains

t `0.2.1-rc.3`.
- A running **decision model API** that speaks `POST /v1/systemone`
(the router defa

ults to `http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/systemone`; edit
`ROUTER_BASE` in `plugin/index.js` to point at an

other host or port).
- `pnpm` on PATH of the host running DSH (the plugin manager installs
through p
npm; the CLI forwards pnpm arguments).

docs and the test suites.

repository root):

**From a prebuilt tarball (plugin panel / GitHub Release):** pick the newest
tag on the Releases pag

e,
then either paste the tarball URL into the panel (**Plugins → Add plugin**):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
or download it and install from the local path:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then select the bundle on the Plugins page (installation enables it by
default) and restart DSH if t
he profile runs without HMR.

**Plugins panel (1.2.0+):** the package ships panel metadata
(`locale/en.json` + `locale/zh.json`, `

icon.svg`, and the matching `exports`
entries), so it renders as the **Tool Router** card with a des

cription and an
icon under your own bundles instead of a bare package name.
## Uninstall

Deselect/remove the bundle on the Plugins page. The preset row and the host
tool flips vanish with t

he bundle patch; other presets are untouched. Note:
with HMR disabled the panel refuses live uninsta

lls ("stop it and uninstall
the package with `dsh plugin`") — either enable the `hmr` row temporaril

y or
use `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @residenthiago/dsh-tool-router`.
## Files
| File | Purpose |
| `plugin/index.js` | The router plugin: registers `find_tool`, masks every other tool per agent, ru

ns the 3-stage decision. |
| `plugin/cordis.patch.yml` | The bundle patch: preset declaration + host

tool enablement. |
